rationale:
bugs_open/223, phase 1 of 2. The landmine-verifier (RFC_005 s3.2) has been reporting footprints as non-existent when the truth is that code_symbols, the index it queries, CANNOT REPRESENT the thing being looked up. Re-measured live 2026-08-10: 5,837 rows, 100% .go, 682 paths, and NO var/const/type row at all despite the table's own CHECK constraint permitting all three. The bug's census stands: 1,116 of 1,371 landmine footprint rows (81%), spanning 284 of 288 entries, can never resolve.

WHY THIS IS NOT A WORDING FIX, which is the objection this round should expect. The bug's own in-file correction is the deciding evidence: on IDENTICAL 0-row input the conclusion varies run to run — four verdicts within one hour on v1.0.1267 ranged from a correct abstention ('cannot be mechanically verified') to a flat 'the entire described workflow has no footprint', asserted about three scripts in this repo, in a doc_notes row written BY those scripts into the category it declared empty. Three of four runs already hedge correctly. So improving the average buys nothing: an entry is degraded by the one flat STALE and the reader cannot tell which run they are holding. The blindness is DETERMINISTIC and knowable before the answer is read; only the inference is stochastic. This change removes the stochastic step's input and then bars the inference structurally.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. (1) A verifier run was dispatched ON PURPOSE this morning, on a landmine this lane had appended minutes earlier whose footprint is almost entirely the unrepresentable class, and its collected_data is banked verbatim in the lane's EVIDENCE file. Five of its eight derived checks were unanswerable BY CONSTRUCTION; the rendered answer said 'The query was RUN; this is not an unanswered question' for each. The scope line stated freshness and body coverage and was silent on the only two facts the run needed. The verdict then reached 'either not present at the current ref OR not indexed' — a disjunction ONE CENSUS would have collapsed — and GUESSED the census correctly ('the index appears Go-centric'), hedging everything on the guess. That is the GOOD branch, and it is still a wasted round. (2) A false-POSITIVE mode the bug does not record: ls is a path-prefix listing over an index of Go symbols and presents as a directory listing. 'scripts/' returns 110 indexed paths (Go programs in subdirectories) while every .py and .sh directly under it is invisible, so a generous listing reads as confirmation that a footprint resolves. That is worse than a false STALE — a wrong accusation invites checking; a flattering partial confirmation reads as diligence. (3) A content check aimed at a non-Go file can be answered by a same-named Go symbol: 'slugify' returned six confident hits on slugifyPathSegments/slugifyForCompositionName, none of them the Python function asked about. A false positive with citations.

WHERE THE DEFECT LIVES, and why the fix is one layer below the agent. The damaging sentence is in the SHARED action, not in the verifier's prompt. emptyAnswer's in-scope branches assert the strongest available reading, and that wording was itself a fix (bugs_closed/108 defect B, where empty answers read as silence) which succeeded and then became the mechanism of the opposite error. A guard can be wrong by being too confident. Placing the correction in answerCodeCheck/emptyAnswer reaches all four consumers of the seam from one edit — fix-proposer, feature-designer, landmine-verifier, and the runtime lane which calls answerCodeCheck directly at diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:479 and whose own comment already states the requirement being generalised: "'0 rows because bodies are not indexed' and '0 rows because the code does not do that' must not render identically." This is the same shape as the three prior fixes in this file (108 freshness, 108 bodies, 163 path:Symbol, 181 row caps), one census along, and it is built on that file's existing precedent (bodyCoverageNote) rather than on a new idea.

EVERY NEW SENTENCE IS COMPUTED FROM A LIVE CENSUS, never hardcoded. A '.go only' string would go on printing after it stopped being true — the stale-status class this estate has scars from. The census is one GROUP BY per action run over (kind, extension); when the corpus widens, the warnings retire themselves, and TestMissingKindNoteDisappears asserts that in advance rather than leaving it to be discovered as stale prose.

THE STRUCTURAL BAR. Four additive return keys carry the census mechanically (nothing consumed them before: measured 0 live definitions referencing any of them, or checks_run). Seed 365 then makes the STALE-bearing prompt UNREACHABLE for a round that confirmed nothing against indexed code, via a conditional_branch on no_code_evidence, and appends the action's own evidence_line to the persisted verdict body through a new OPT-IN append_doc_note key. That last part is the load-bearing half for a reader six months out: the verifier's product is prose in doc_notes that nothing parses, read by sessions and by council seats' schema_hint, so the qualifier must be attached by machinery that the model whose verdict it qualifies cannot soften, contradict or omit.

SCOPE, honestly. This does NOT fix the var/const blind spot itself — bugs_open/231's class (a hypothesis whose deciding evidence is the CONTENT of a package-level var) still stops at UNVERIFIABLE. It now stops honestly, naming the index as the limit instead of inventing 'possibly inlined or renamed'. Indexing those kinds is phase 2: measured at 1,173 package-level specs (~+20% corpus), it changes every diagnosis run's search space plus embeddings and prune cohorts, so it gets its own commit and its own round. Ingesting non-Go files is excluded entirely as architecture-scope by the 2026-07-29 ruling, as the bug itself says.

NO ORDERING CONSTRAINT IS CLAIMED (owner ruling 2026-07-29, condition 1 retired). The seed is safe before the image rolls and this was verified rather than assumed: conditional_branch resolves an absent field to nil (resolveFieldValue) and compareValues(nil,'true') is false, so on the current binary the gate takes else_step and behaves exactly as today, with no error path; and append_doc_note declares neither ConfigKeys nor CheckConfig nor StrictConfig, so it is not opted into unknown-config-key detection and the new key is inert, not even a warning. The degraded window is 'no gate and no evidence suffix until the roll', which is today's behaviour. Registration in the same commit (DIAG-036 capability change + new DIAG-042) satisfies the surviving condition (2).

plan.summary: Teach the shared code-lookup action what its corpus CANNOT represent, derived from a live census rather than hardcoded, so a 0-row answer for an unrepresentable class renders NOT ANSWERABLE BY THIS INDEX instead of 'the query was RUN; this is not an unanswered question' — and a non-empty `ls` listing says what it is a listing OF, which is the false-positive half. Carry the same facts mechanically in four additive return keys, then use them in the landmine-verifier's workflow to make STALE UNREACHABLE for a round that confirmed nothing against indexed code, and to append the action's own evidence census to every persisted verdict through a new opt-in append_doc_note key. Four consumers benefit from the Go edit; only the verifier's config changes. Indexing Go var/const is phase 2, its own commit and round; ingesting non-Go files is excluded as architecture-scope.

edits.rationale: The census is the load-bearing fact every new sentence derives from, and this struct already exists for exactly this purpose — it is how bugs_closed/108's 'answered 0 rows, searched N symbols' and the bodies-not-indexed note are computed. Adding per-extension and per-kind counts is its third widening, not a new mechanism. It must be READ rather than written down: a hardcoded '.go only' would keep printing after the corpus widened, which is the stale-status class. The census read is deliberately NON-fatal and does NOT set s.err — s.err means 'we know nothing about scope' and would suppress the older guards that depend on the row counts. A partial read discards both maps rather than keeping half, because a half-read census would report an extension as absent because iteration stopped, which is the exact false 'does not exist' being fixed.

edits.symbol: unanswerableReason / notAnswerableAnswer / emptyAnswer / lsReachNote / contentReachNote / missingKindNote
edits.rationale: The classification must travel WITH the data (bugs_closed/108's principle: the prompt telling a reader to treat an empty answer as unknown is not in front of them when they read it), and it must be PER CHECK because a mixed footprint is the dangerous case — a partly-confirmed verdict reads as diligent. CONSERVATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, in the same direction as looksLikePath: it speaks only about a file extension the census says is absent, so a directory prefix, a bare identifier, free text, or an unknown census all keep the pre-223 wording. A false NOT ANSWERABLE would suppress a real absence, which is the mirror of the bug. The lsReachNote is the one caveat that rides on a NON-EMPTY answer, because `ls` advertises a directory listing and delivers a Go-file listing. missingKindNote is what removes the invented 'possibly inlined or renamed': the absent KIND becomes a stated fact rather than a gap the model explains.

checks_run counts checks that EXECUTED and cannot distinguish 'ran, found rows' from 'ran, found nothing' — so no consumer could branch on evidence, and the bug's conclusion is that only a structural bar removes the bad inference. answerCodeCheck therefore returns what it ESTABLISHED, not only prose. codeRows counts CODE-TIER rows only: the D12 guard exists because a document SAYS where only code SHOWS, and a field named 'did this find evidence' must honour the same line or it launders prose into proof one layer up. The three states (rows / unanswerable / ran-and-found-nothing) are kept distinct because collapsing them into a boolean is how 'no rows' became 'does not exist' in the first place. codeEvidenceLine is composed HERE so that no model writes, softens or omits it. The row-cap invariant (bugs_open/181) is untouched: every arm still binds probeLimit(rowCap) and renders rowCapNotice from an OBSERVED probe row, and the new rendering replaces only the 0-row branch, which is mutually exclusive with capped.

The runtime lane calls answerCodeCheck directly — deliberate reuse, per its own comment, so that one guard covers the council tier and this lane alike — and the widened signature forces the update. It gets the same protection, which it needs at least as much: its verdict prompt's cite-or-abstain acts on absence, and bugs_open/231 is the recorded case where a 090 run stopped at UNVERIFIABLE naming 'the actual var declaration … is NOT in the bundle' — true, unfixable by re-running, and never stated to it as a property of the corpus rather than of the code. This consumer is invisible to any agent_definitions query, which is why it is named explicitly here.

The only mechanical way to attach the evidence census to the PERSISTED row: note_body_field is a single field, and no compose action exists (transform_data was read and is legacy — it reads validate_input/input_data, not arbitrary collected fields). This is the load-bearing half for a reader six months out, because the verifier's product is prose that nothing parses, and a caveat the model is merely ASKED to include arrives most of the time — which is exactly the property that makes the failures expensive. OPT-IN with the unsafe default OFF, per the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 §2: absent from a step's config the action behaves byte-identically, so no other consumer of this shared action changes, and adoption is visible at each call site instead of asserted in a comment. An EMPTY resolution is stated loudly IN the row rather than skipped, because a missing qualifier is precisely the condition the key exists to make visible; the suffix is applied after the empty-body refusal so it can never make an empty verdict look written.

The structural bar, expressed as workflow TOPOLOGY rather than as prompt hope: run_checks → gate_evidence (conditional_branch on lookup.no_code_evidence) → {verify_unverifiable | verify}. A round that confirmed nothing against indexed code cannot REACH the STALE-bearing prompt. STILL_VALID is absent from that branch too, because the bug records that with zero checkable evidence both directions are uninformative and a STILL_VALID earned by prose reasoning has already been mistaken for verification. The evidence branch keeps its full vocabulary and gains four rules bounding what a STALE may rest on — the MIXED-footprint case, which the bug names as the dangerous one. persist_verdict gains the suffix key. Verification is a DO block that RAISEs, not a list of SELECTs: ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result, so a SELECT-only verify block cannot stop the COMMIT (RFC_006's recorded trap). It asserts the topology AND that STALE is absent from the new branch's vocabulary — checking the wiring without checking that would pass a seed whose new prompt still offered the verdict the branch exists to remove. Snapshot taken before writing; the ROLLBACK restores FROM that snapshot rather than string-trimming the appended text, because another lane may have amended the same prompt since and trimming would silently discard their work.
edits.sketch:
run_checks.next_step            → "gate_evidence"
gate_evidence                   → conditional_branch {condition: "lookup.no_code_evidence == true",
                                   then_step: "verify_unverifiable", else_step: "verify"}
verify_unverifiable             → execute_llm_prompt, status ∈ {UNVERIFIABLE, NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW}
                                   "An index that cannot represent a footprint tells you NOTHING about
                                    whether it exists, was removed, was renamed or was inlined."
verify.config.prompt_template   → || EVIDENCE RULES (a NOT ANSWERABLE line is evidence in NEITHER
                                   direction; STALE only on rows that contradict, or an in-scope 0;
                                   no rename claim without a row showing where it went)
persist_verdict.config          → + note_body_suffix_field: "lookup.evidence_line"
DO $$ … RAISE EXCEPTION on any of: wrong next_step, missing branch, missing suffix,
        STALE still in the no-evidence vocabulary, EVIDENCE RULES applied twice $$

edits.rationale: The file's existing tests are pure-function (freshnessBanner, emptyAnswer, mixedCommitNote), and this adds sqlmock WIRING tests beside them — BECAUSE A MUTATION SURVIVED. Silencing b.WriteString(scope.lsReachNote()) to b.WriteString("") killed no test in the first version: the suite exercised the helpers and nothing asserted the call sites, so the false-positive half of the fix — the half not recorded in the bug — was the half left unprotected. A helper with no caller looks exactly like a finished fix. Every guard now dies under a named mutation: invert representsExt (classification fails both ways), drop missingKindNote from emptyAnswer, silence lsReachNote at the CALL SITE, unwire notAnswerableAnswer in an arm, under-report unanswerable in the evidence line, count doc rows as evidence in the content arm, no-op applyBodySuffix. TestMissingKindNoteDisappears asserts phase 2's self-erasure IN ADVANCE — a census-driven renderer can prove that negative where a mock's own bookkeeping cannot. TestLsArmKeepsHonestAbsenceForAnIndexedExtension is the test that fails if the fix ever starts buying abstention by classifying more than it should. No existing assertion was weakened: the pre-existing tests pass unchanged because their scope fixture carries no census, which is the fail-open path working as designed.

edits.rationale: Registration in the SAME commit that ships the seam is the surviving condition (2) of the 2026-07-29 ordering ruling. DIAG-036 takes a CAPABILITY CHANGE note beside 163's, because this is the same family one layer along — 163 made a well-formed query satisfiable, this states that the CORPUS rather than the predicate is what emptied an answer. A new DIAG-042 records the evidence-gated verdict topology and the note_body_suffix_field seam. Both carry their landmines: (a) checks_run > 0 does NOT mean anything was verified — branch on no_code_evidence, or the pre-223 failure returns with new field names; (b) a test suite over the rendering helpers passes while the fix is unwired, so mutate the CALL SITE; (c) note_body_suffix_field resolving empty writes a loud line by design — do not 'fix' it to fail quiet. The entry also states what this does NOT fix (231's var-content class still stops at UNVERIFIABLE, honestly now) so nobody reads coverage into it, and records the deliberately-excluded external check classes as the open review question — including that the git class CANNOT run in this action, because the shared chassis pod holds no GitHub read token by design.

grounded_in: bugs_open/223, its own CORRECTION: 'the defect is one layer up from where I filed it. The blind spot is *deterministic*; the **inference drawn from it is stochastic**, ranging from a correct abstention to a flat assertion of non-existence, with nothing binding the conclusion to the blindness.'

bugs_open/223: 'Ask the model to abstain when it cannot check is already what it does *most* of the time — 3 of 4 verdicts here — and the failure mode is precisely that you cannot tell which run you got. An entry is degraded by the one flat STALE, not rescued by the three careful ones. **Only a structural bar on the inference removes it.**'

bugs_open/223, candidate 4 rejected: 'Suppress the verdict wording only … Rejected as a stand-alone: it treats a false conclusion as a phrasing problem, and WRONG_CALLS.md has a standing entry on exactly that move.'

The live verdict this bug was filed on: 'None of the three scripts (landmines-sync.py, landmines-verify-dispatch.sh, trigger-landmine-verifier.sh), the --apply flag, the NEEDS_VERIFICATION: output, or the landmine-verification category exist anywhere in the indexed codebase; the entire described workflow has no footprint.' — written BY that toolchain, INTO that category.

Re-measured live 2026-08-10: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE path LIKE '%.go'), count(*) FILTER (WHERE path NOT LIKE '%.go'), count(*) FROM code_symbols → 5837 / 0 / 5837 across 682 paths; SELECT kind, count(*) … GROUP BY 1 → func 3653, method 1119, struct 987, alias 42, interface 36 — no var, const or type row, while the table's own constraint permits all three: CHECK (kind = ANY (ARRAY['func','method','struct','interface','alias','type','var','const'])).

A run dispatched by this lane on purpose, 2026-08-10 10:58Z, v1.0.1277, banked verbatim: '[code_check 1] kind=ls query="scripts/landmines_lib.py" … answered: 0 rows — no indexed path has that prefix, out of 5837 indexed symbols. The query was RUN; this is not an unanswered question.' Five of its eight checks were unanswerable by construction.

The same run's verdict, the CAREFUL branch, still a total loss: 'returned 0 rows in the code_symbols index (checks 1 and 3), meaning they are either not present at the current ref or not indexed (the index covers Go symbols heavily but may not cover Python scripts) … there is no way to confirm or deny that the described behavior still holds.' — a disjunction one census collapses, resolved by GUESSING the census.

The false-positive mode, measured 2026-08-10: SELECT count(*) FROM code_symbols WHERE path LIKE 'scripts/%' → 110 (scripts/documentation_project/01/analyser.go, scripts/goscripts/…), while every .py and .sh directly under scripts/ is absent. An ls check at directory altitude returns a generous listing that reads as confirmation.

The same run's check 2, a false positive WITH citations: kind=content query="slugify" — 'confirms the slugify function exists in landmines_lib.py' — returned six Go rows (slugifyPathSegments in adopt_verbatim.go, slugifyForCompositionName in resolve_composition_helpers.go), none of them the Python function.

diagnose_load_runtime_action.go, the fourth consumer's own comment, stating the requirement being generalised: 'the verdict prompt's cite-or-abstain acts on absence, so "0 rows because bodies are not indexed" and "0 rows because the code does not do that" must not render identically. Same helper as diagnose_code_lookup — one judgement, not a sibling copy that drifts (016b §9).'

bugs_open/223's third failure mode, on a live Go var: 'metaCommentaryPatterns and placeholderPatterns no longer resolve as standalone symbols (possibly inlined or renamed)' — both exist at HEAD, unrenamed, at validate_page_content.go:105 and :1229; code_symbols holds no var kind at all. 'The phrasing manufactures a hypothesis the evidence never supported.'

bugs_open/223's 2026-08-09 addendum, the second consumer of the same blindness: a 090 run 'stopped at UNVERIFIABLE with this as its stated gap 1: the actual var declaration of DeployImageAssetInputSpec — specifically its Defaults map — is NOT in the bundle … Whoever fixes this bug's lookup layer fixes both consumers at once.'

bugs_open/223's scope census: '1,116 of 1,371 footprint rows (81%) can never be resolved, spanning 284 of 288 entries … a mixed entry is the dangerous one, because a partly-confirmed verdict reads as diligent.'

Key-collision measurement before adding them, 2026-08-10: 0 rows from SELECT count(*) FROM agent_definitions WHERE default_config::text LIKE ANY(ARRAY['%no_code_evidence%','%checks_with_rows%','%checks_unanswerable%','%evidence_line%','%note_body_suffix_field%']) AND deleted_at IS NULL; and 0 definitions reference checks_run.

Pre-roll safety, verified in the code rather than assumed: conditional_branch_action.go's resolveFieldValue returns nil for an absent field with no error, and compareValues(nil,"true") returns 'expected == "null" || "nil" || ""' = false ⇒ else_step. AppendDocNoteInputSpec declares no ConfigKeys, no CheckConfig and no StrictConfig, so per action_inputs.go it is 'not checked at all' for unknown config keys.

The consumers this seam is shared with, enumerated 2026-08-10: SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE default_config::text LIKE '%diagnose_code_lookup%' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL → fix-proposer, feature-designer, landmine-verifier; plus answerCodeCheck's direct Go caller at diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:479, which no DB query can see.

Baseline on the running binary with a negative control, 2026-08-10, both replicas v1.0.1277: 'this answer is CAPPED' → 1, '0 rows AT THAT PATH' → 1, 'source BODIES ARE NOT INDEXED' → 1, 'NOT ANSWERABLE BY THIS INDEX' → 0.

Owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2, the shape this fix's new authority takes: 'when a seam's widest branch is licensed by "callers must all be X", make X a field with the unsafe default OFF … A comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share.'

Owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2, on what may be claimed here: 'The only mechanism that actually holds a seam back is a default-OFF switch … So: review here is after the fact, by design. Do not claim an ordering constraint you do not have.' Condition (2), registration in the same commit, is satisfied by the DIAG-036/DIAG-042 edit.
plan.risks:
1. A false NOT ANSWERABLE would suppress a real absence — the mirror of the bug. Contained by making the classifier speak only about a file extension the census says is absent: a directory prefix, a bare identifier, free text, an unknown census and any represented extension all keep the pre-223 wording. TestUnanswerableReasonIsConservative and TestLsArmKeepsHonestAbsenceForAnIndexedExtension assert exactly this, and inverting representsExt fails them in both directions.

2. The census read is a second query per action run. Non-fatal by construction and it does not set s.err (which would suppress the older guards); a failure or partial read degrades to 'composition unknown', which the classifier treats as 'claim nothing'. Cost is one GROUP BY over a 5,837-row table, on an action that already runs up to 10 indexed lookups.

3. Three other consumers of the seam see changed ANSWER TEXT (fix-proposer, feature-designer, the runtime lane). No consumer parses that text mechanically — 0 definitions reference checks_run, measured — and for an in-corpus query the wording is unchanged, so the delta is a caveat added where a caveat was owed. They are named in this rationale and get a dated note in bugs_open/223; the runtime lane's own comment already asked for this.

4. Verdict VOCABULARY changes on the no-evidence branch (UNVERIFIABLE appears; STALE and STILL_VALID cannot). Nothing parses verdict status — it is prose in doc_notes read by humans, sessions and council schema_hint — but RFC_005 §3.2 is architecture_review's mechanism, so they are named as an owner to tell rather than merely measured.

5. The evidence suffix lands on EVERY landmine verdict once seed 365 applies, including well-evidenced ones. Deliberate: a qualifier that appears only on bad verdicts would be a signal the model could learn to avoid triggering, and a reader cannot calibrate a caveat they only ever see in one condition.

6. PHASE 2 (var/const indexing) is NOT in this round and its risks are not claimed here: ~1,173 new specs (+20% corpus), one-off embedding cost, a new prune cohort that reads 0%-confirmed on a mixed-binary fleet and therefore REFUSES the whole prune (safe direction, self-healing, visible in doc_notes), and a changed retrieval search space for every diagnosis run. Own commit, own round.

7. Ingesting non-Go files is EXCLUDED as architecture-scope per the 2026-07-29 ruling and the bug's own candidate 3. Evidence it is a separate intent rather than an oversight: the reader-side D12 guard (kindDoc, docBlockHeader) is built and inert, and code_symbols' CHECK constraint does not admit 'doc' — so ingestion needs a schema change, i.e. its own lane by construction.
